brief.headline: New evening confusion reported 2026-10-01, including a stove left on, started about two weeks after a 2026-09-12 ED visit. The notes don't show whether the planned work-up was done.

items.statement: On 2026-10-01 the RN documented that Marcus reports Winford has been more confused in the evenings for about two weeks. He was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. Plan was urinalysis, medication review, and a PCP visit that week.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 2026-10-01 RN note.

items.statement: Safety concern: Winford once left the stove on (reported 2026-10-01). No note in this period records a safety follow-up, such as a home safety review or supervision of cooking.
items.verifier_note: The stove report is in the 10-01 note. The cited notes (10-11 RN check, 10-12 aide visit) don't mention any safety follow-up, so the absence claim is consistent with them.

items.statement: No urinalysis result, medication review, or PCP visit following the 2026-10-01 plan appears in the notes provided. Later notes (2026-10-11 RN check, 2026-10-12 aide visit) say "no new concerns" or "good spirits" and do not mention the confusion. The 2026-09-18, 09-19 and 09-24 notes describe him as at baseline or stable, before the confusion was reported.
items.verifier_note: The notes match the statement. The 10-11 and 10-12 notes say 'no new concerns' and 'good spirits' and don't mention confusion. The 09-18, 09-19 and 09-24 notes describe baseline or stable status. No UA, medication review or PCP visit appears in the cited notes.

items.statement: ED visit on 2026-09-12 for COPD exacerbation. He was treated and released the same day, with follow-up with PACE primary care advised within 7 days. The PCP post-hospital visit on 2026-09-18 found him back to baseline per his niece.
items.verifier_note: The ED visit, same-day release, 7-day follow-up advice, and the 09-18 PCP note (back to baseline per niece) are all in the sources.

items.statement: A prednisone 40 mg short course ran 2026-09-12 to 2026-09-17 after the ED visit. The reported evening confusion began roughly mid-September, around the time of this course. The active medication list shows only the fluticasone and albuterol inhalers.
items.verifier_note: The prednisone 40 mg course from 09-12 to 09-17 is supported. The onset of confusion is roughly mid-September (about two weeks before 10-01), which is a fair inference. However, the claim that the active medication list shows only the fluticasone and albuterol inhalers isn't in the cited sources; the medication record lists only the prednisone start.

items.statement: No flu vaccine is recorded for the current season (began 2026-08-01). The last influenza vaccine was 2026-01-28.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows flu_vaccine_this_season false, a season start of 2026-08-01, and a last influenza vaccine on 2026-01-28.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and the last IDT review date; pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions in the window, including any sepsis-related presentations given the history of sepsis (2000).
Falls and near-falls check: any reported falls, fall-related injuries, or fall-risk screening changes in the window, since the participant is 73 with obesity and possible diabetes-related risks.

Medication reconciliation: compare active list (fluticasone propionate 44 mcg MDI and albuterol HFA MDI, both started 2026-01-28) against pharmacy fills and any new starts or stops in the window. Note that no diabetes, lipid, or blood pressure medications appear on the active list despite the type 2 diabetes diagnosis (2025-01-22) and hypertriglyceridemia/metabolic syndrome (2026-01-28); flag for the team to confirm whether this reflects an omission, a non-pharmacologic plan, or outside prescribing.

Diabetes monitoring: review most recent HbA1c, fasting or random glucose values, any glucose-lowering prescriptions considered or started, hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia events, and whether eye exam, foot exam, urine albumin, and kidney function (eGFR/creatinine) are due or completed.
Lipids and metabolic syndrome: review triglyceride, HDL, LDL, and waist or BMI trend since the 2026-01-28 diagnoses; confirm whether a lipid-related plan or referral was documented.
Weight and BMI trend across the window (obesity is a long-standing condition); flag gain or loss of 5 percent or more and any dietary or activity referrals.
Blood pressure readings in the window, since hypertension is not listed but metabolic syndrome criteria include BP; flag any readings above the team's threshold and confirm whether BP was rechecked.

Respiratory status: asthma control in the window, including albuterol rescue inhaler use frequency, nighttime symptoms, steroid bursts or oral steroid courses, exacerbation visits, oxygen saturation trends, and inhaler technique or adherence to fluticasone.
Anemia follow-up: review the most recent hemoglobin or CBC, any iron or B12 studies, and whether a workup or treatment change is pending, since anemia has been on the problem list since 1984.

Function, cognition, mood, and social: ADL and IADL changes, cognitive screen results or concerns, depression screen (PHQ-2 or PHQ-9) scores, social isolation or caregiver strain, transportation barriers to visits, and whether any care-plan items (assessments, goals, referrals, advance care planning) are due or overdue as of 2026-11-30.
